title: TokenPB: Enabling VLA Action Self-Verification via VLM Token Probability Bucketing
claim: Adding an auxiliary objective alongside the main loss speeds up optimization and gives higher downstream success at every training checkpoint.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left loss curves, right success-rate curves with shaded bands
description: Two line plots sit side by side. The left plot shows flow-matching loss (log-like y-axis, 0 to 1.2) against training step (0 to 30k). A blue noisy curve for L_fm only and an orange curve for the joint L_fm + β L_bucket (TokenPB co-training) both fall steeply. The orange curve drops faster and stays lower, at about 0.01–0.02 against about 0.04 for blue. A legend sits at the top. The right plot shows success rate (%) against step, with three curves and shaded variance bands. A navy curve with circles is the joint-trained model evaluated with TokenPB at M=16. A gold curve with squares is the joint-trained model evaluated single-sample. A purple curve with triangles is the L_fm-only model evaluated single-sample. The navy curve is highest, gold is in the middle, and purple is lowest. All curves converge near 95–100% at 30k. The legend is at the lower right.
caption: Bucket co-training improves optimization and success. Left: adding Lbucket alongside the flow-matching loss Lfm accelerates convergence (lower Lfm at the same step). Right: at every checkpoint, joint training (Lfm + β Lbucket) yields higher downstream success rates than the Lfm-only baseline.
abstract: Test-time sampling can improve Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but only if the model can efficiently select a good action from multiple candidates. Prior work often relies on separately trained external verifiers, adding extra models and inference overhead. We propose \textbf{Token Probability Bucketing (TokenPB)}, a self-verification approach that discretizes continuous action chunks into bucket tokens and co-trains a single VLA checkpoint with a joint objective: a flow-matching loss for action generation and an auxiliary bucket loss $\mathcal{L}_{\text{bucket}}$ that teaches the VLM backbone to model observation-conditioned distributions over bucket-token sequences. At inference, TokenPB samples $M$ candidates, scores each via teacher-forced evaluation under the learned distribution, and selects the best---enabling efficient batched scoring with observation-prefix KV-cache reuse. We provide theory connecting the training objective to a monotonic ranking property and bounds on expected selection regret that separate candidate-set effects from calibration. Across multiple backbones and benchmarks, TokenPB yields consistent success-rate improvements over single-sample inference from the same checkpoint (+2.7 in simulation, +17.1 in real-world, +16.4 under out-of-distribution shifts), and further improves over external-verifier baselines under the same sampling budget. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/RUCKBReasoning/TokenPB.
